assessment: The incumbent appears effective for stable course assignments: 24 such files had seven-minute median handling, a concrete limit on any account blaming CSV export generally. Overall course-set accuracy was 32/40 and median handling 17 minutes, missing both targets. Assignment changes and renames cluster among affected exports, but this does not establish causation or the authoritative intended set. Fast execution alongside long replacement waits suggests a separate delay. Zero observed cross-center rows does not establish isolation for the unsampled split-course case. All observations are stipulated synthetic evidence.

openings.claim: Using current assignments or names to resolve a requested week's courses may explain some apparent omissions; stable course identity plus week-relevant assignment resolution could reduce them.
openings.delta: Make the export's course-set interpretation explicit and test temporal resolution before changing scheduling.
openings.prediction: Against coordinator-agreed intended sets, week-relevant resolution corrects assignment-change discrepancies while unchanged-course results remain stable; rename-only discrepancies distinguish identity handling from assignment timing.
openings.probe: In fabricated staging, compare current and proposed resolution for unchanged, reassigned, renamed, and split courses across two centers. Confirm intended sets with consenting coordinators, compare actual CSV contents, test import compatibility and concurrent attendance entry, and reject deployment if effort or hosting exceeds the bound.
assumptions: Historical assignments and stable identities are available or recoverable within six engineer-days.
Coordinator agreement supplies a usable intended-set reference.
All processing stays within the private service and authorized workspaces.

openings.claim: Does coordinator-controlled regeneration reduce active handling enough to affect the target, or does it primarily shorten elapsed waiting?
openings.delta: Separate replacement delay from the measured handling burden before prioritizing a regeneration control.
openings.prediction: If replacement coordination drives handling, immediate regeneration reduces active minutes; if spreadsheet checking or import dominates, elapsed turnaround improves while active minutes change little.
openings.probe: Use two short sessions per consenting coordinator with counterbalanced fabricated replacement tasks. Compare the current request workflow with a simulated private regeneration control; record active checking, requesting, downloading, importing, and elapsed waiting separately. Preserve CSV schema, center scope, and attendance entry.
assumptions: The bounded simulation fits existing resources.
Session timings diagnose components but do not establish the next-40-export success rate.
